title: Harden Dedicated & Private observability: local agent shims + tenant-scoped pipelines
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Goal: Provide robust, tenant-isolated telemetry for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments using a small local agent shim plus tenant-scoped pipeline configurations. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout for: 1) trace/span tagging and propagation hooks in the local shim, 2) tenant-scoped metric/log pipelines that prevent cross-tenant leakage, and 3) a fallback sharding policy when central collectors are unreachable in air-gapped or low-bandwidth environments.

Background: Customers running Dedicated/Private want parity with hosted observability (traces, metrics, logs, dashboards) but with strict isolation and limited egress. The hosted collector architecture can't be used directly in VPC/on-prem without re-architecting how we annotate and route telemetry. Previous incidents showed misattributed traces when collector-side routing rules lacked tenant metadata (incident learnings linked below).

Success criteria / acceptance: 
- All telemetry emitted from Dedicated/Private nodes includes a cryptographically verifiable tenant_id and org_namespace header.
- Local agent shim correctly enriches spans and metrics and signs tenant metadata for downstream pipeline verification.
- Pipeline configs support per-tenant routing to customer-owned destinations (S3, Splunk, private Elasticsearch) with no cross-tenant buffering.
- End-to-end test suite (integration tests in CI) validates isolation under collector failover and network partitions.
- New dashboards in Console-ops showing per-tenant ingestion rate, tail latency, error rate, and pipeline backpressure (release: runtime-1.20).

Design summary: 
- Local agent shim (lightweight Go binary) runs beside runtime in Dedicated/Private nodes. It provides: automatic tagging (tenant_id, deployment_id, region), trace context enrichment hooks, and an agent-level buffer with tenant-aware sharding.
- Pipelines are templated and deployed per-tenant in the private control plane. Templates include verification steps that validate signed tenant metadata before accepting events.
- When central collector unreachable, shim enters isolated-forwarding mode: it persists encrypted batches to local disk (configurable retention) and optionally forwards to a customer-configured sink. The shim exposes a scrape endpoint for on-site debug (auth via mTLS).

Trade-offs considered: 
- Agent vs. sidecar: An in-process library would be lower latency but risks leaking secrets and requires per-language SDK changes. We chose an external shim to centralize signing logic and to avoid SDK churn.
- On-disk buffering vs. immediate drop: Keeping local encrypted buffer avoids data loss but requires disk space management and adds complexity for retention policies; default policy is bounded queue with configurable retention and eviction (LRU by tenant precedence).
- Verification complexity: End-to-end cryptographic signatures add CPU overhead; we limit verification to pipeline ingress nodes and batch-verify where possible.

Rollout plan: 
1) Alpha: deploy shim to a small fleet of Dedicated customers (opt-in) with debug-level logging. Validate tagging and signing. (2 weeks)
2) Beta: enable tenant-scoped pipelines for customers with on-prem collectors; add CI integration tests, security review. (3 weeks)
3) GA: expose configuration in Console (pipeline templates and retention controls) + runtime-1.20 release. (2 weeks)

Testing & validation: 
- Unit tests for signing/enrichment logic.
- Integration test harness simulating collector network partitions and verifying no cross-tenant leakage.
- Load test verifying latency P95 for trace emission remains within 10% of hosted baseline.
- Manual security pen-test of shim and pipeline verification.

Monitoring and dashboards: 
- New Console-ops dashboards: per-tenant ingestion counters, signed-metadata verification failure rate, shim local-queue utilization, pipeline backpressure latency, and delivery success/failure histogram.
- Alerts: verification-failure-rate > 0.1% for > 5m (P0 alert), local-queue usage > 80% for > 10m (warning).

Open questions: 
- Key management: should tenant signing keys be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) in Private deployments? Proposal: support both — default platform-managed with opt-in BYOK.
- Backpressure semantics across multi-tenant buffer: eviction policy must balance fairness vs. SLA tiers.

Documentation and runbooks: 
- Confluence design doc (link below).
- Runbook for local shim: start/stop, disk cleanup, forced-forward mode.

Links to artifacts and context: see links field for PRs, incident notes, and dashboards.

Owners: Aisha Patel (eng lead), Daniel Kim (platform architect).
comments: 2025-01-11 | Daniel Kim: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence. Agreed to start with an external shim rather than in-process instrumentation. Action: prototype shim that adds tenant metadata to OpenTelemetry spans.

2025-01-17 | Aisha Patel: Prototype completed. Observed ~4% increase in CPU at peak with batch signing enabled — acceptable for targeted Dedicated SKUs. Pushed initial PoC at https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-shim/pull/19.

2025-01-21 | Security Review (Lena Sørensen): Requested BYOK design and threat model for local disk encryption. Security review flagged need for mTLS between shim and control plane. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-01-25 | QA (Ravi Desai): Integration tests added to CI. Failure case found: when collector DNS flaps, shim retried aggressively; added exponential backoff and jitter. PT: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-shim/pull/27.
2025-02-03 | Aisha Patel: Beta rollout smoke test passed for 3 pilot customers. Dashboard queries and example Grafana panels posted to internal dashboard library. Scheduling GA docs for 2025-02-14.
